2608.13515.title: Measuring Task-Agnostic Training Data Influence Across Language Model Pretraining
2608.13515.paper_summary: Measuring training data influence consistently across language model pretraining is challenging. It is difficult to select downstream tasks or validation sets representative of a model's general capabilities, and reliance on task performance at intermediate checkpoints complicates comparisons across training. We propose a measure of training data influence that does not require selecting a downstream task or validation set as the attribution target. Specifically, we define an example's influence by how much its gradient update reduces the squared distance to the final parameters of a given pretraining run, and estimate this quantity from intermediate checkpoints without retraining. Applying the method to 18 configurations from the Pythia and PolyPythia suites, we find systematic temporal changes in influential data. Early in training, literature-related data are more strongly aligned with the trajectory toward the final parameters, whereas STEM data become more strongly aligned in later stages. This qualitative crossover is broadly consistent across model configurations. Our results provide a tractable trajectory-level view of how influential data change throughout pretraining, complementing influence analyses defined with respect to specific downstream tasks or validation sets.
2608.13515.paper_summary_zh: 測量訓練數據在語言模型預訓練中的影響是一項挑戰。選擇能代表模型一般能力的下游任務或驗證集是困難的，而依賴中間檢查點的任務表現則使得跨訓練的比較變得複雜。我們提出了一種訓練數據影響的度量，這不需要選擇下游任務或驗證集作為歸因目標。具體而言，我們通過一個示例的梯度更新減少到給定預訓練運行的最終參數的平方距離來定義其影響，並從中間檢查點估計這個量，而不需要重新訓練。將該方法應用於 Pythia 和 PolyPythia 套件的 18 種配置，我們發現有影響力的數據在時間上的系統性變化。在訓練的早期，與文獻相關的數據與最終參數的軌跡更強烈地對齊，而 STEM 數據在後期階段則變得更強烈對齊。這種質量上的交叉在模型配置中廣泛一致。我們的結果提供了一個可處理的軌跡級別視角，展示了在預訓練過程中有影響力的數據如何變化，補充了針對特定下游任務或驗證集定義的影響分析。
